text: A rigid designator is a term that picks out a different object in each possible world, depending on which object best satisfies an associated description there.
explanation: False. A rigid designator picks out the same object in every possible world where that object exists; the description given here characterizes a non-rigid designator such as 'the teacher of Alexander,' which can pick out different individuals at different worlds. Kripke's thesis that ordinary names are rigid is what drives his necessity-of-identity and necessary-a-posteriori results.
